o: State purposes of commonly used network protocols.
Compare secure web access and email protocols.
c: Communication protocols are agreed rules controlling how data is exchanged across a network.
HTTP transfers web pages; HTTPS uses encryption for secure web communication; FTP is used for file transfer.
SMTP sends email; POP downloads email to a client; IMAP accesses and synchronises server-based mail across devices.
TCP helps ensure reliable, ordered delivery. IP supports addressing and routing so packets reach the intended destination.

m.title: Email on two devices
m.q: A teacher sends an email on a laptop, then reads received messages on a phone. Explain the roles of SMTP and IMAP. [4 marks]
st: Sending and accessing messages are two separate jobs.
SMTP is used to send outgoing email [1] from client towards email server [1].
IMAP accesses mail stored on a server [1], allowing messages to be synchronised across devices [1].
Name each protocol and link it to the specific email action.

w: A student visits a website requiring login details. Explain why HTTPS is preferable to HTTP. [4 marks]
HTTPS carries web data [1] using encryption [1], making captured traffic unreadable without the key [1] and better protecting sensitive information during transfer [1].
A student uses an email app on several devices. Explain the difference between POP and IMAP. [4 marks]
POP retrieves/downloads mail to a client [1], often for local storage [1]. IMAP keeps/accesses mail on the server [1] and synchronises changes across multiple devices [1].
Describe the different roles of TCP and IP in sending data. [4 marks]
TCP helps ensure reliable delivery [1] in the correct order [1]; IP supplies addressing [1] and routing to the destination across networks [1].
wSteps: Identify what is sent and the security risk.
HTTPS adds encryption to web communication [2].
Encrypted intercepted content is unreadable without the key [2].
HTTPS carries web data [1] using encryption [1], making captured traffic unreadable without the key [1] and better protecting sensitive information during transfer [1].
Differentiate downloaded mail from synchronised remote mail.
POP downloads messages [1]; IMAP accesses server-based mail [1].
POP favours local copies [1]; IMAP keeps devices synchronised [1].
POP retrieves/downloads mail to a client [1], often for local storage [1]. IMAP keeps/accesses mail on the server [1] and synchronises changes across multiple devices [1].
Think reliable arrival versus where the data should go.
TCP helps ensure reliable delivery [1] in the correct order [1]; IP supplies addressing [1] and routing to the destination across networks [1].

k.q: Simulate selecting an encrypted website connection using a number flag.
k.code:
secure = 1
if secure > 0 then
    print("Use HTTPS")
else
    print("Use HTTP")
endif
p: Add print("Protocol chosen") after the decision.
k.a:
Original: Use HTTPS. With 0: Use HTTP.

Extended OCR ERL:
secure = 0
if secure > 0 then
    print("Use HTTPS")
else
    print("Use HTTP")
endif
print("Protocol chosen")

Outputs: Use HTTP; Protocol chosen. The code does not encrypt or connect to a real site.

Source: Original J277-style question; not an OCR past-paper original.

HTTP is used to transfer web resources [1]. HTTPS adds encryption to web communication [1], so an interceptor without the appropriate key cannot read captured payment data [1], protecting sensitive information in transit [1].

Describe the uses of FTP, SMTP, IMAP, TCP and IP. [6 marks]

Source: Original J277-style question; not an OCR past-paper original.

FTP transfers files [1], SMTP sends mail [1], IMAP accesses/synchronises received mail [1], TCP checks reliable and in-order delivery [1], IP addresses packets [1] and routes them between networks [1].
v: Hypertext Transfer Protocol, transfers web resources.
Email-retrieval protocol often downloading mail locally.
Email protocol for accessing and synchronising server-based email.
Supports addressing and routing between networks.
x: SMTP is mainly used to send emails.
r: State one role of an IP address. [1 mark]
Identifies a network destination/used for routing [1].
State one disadvantage of wireless transmission. [1 mark]
Interference, interception/security risk or variable signal quality [1].
State one advantage of a mesh topology. [1 mark]

A pupil cannot open a cloud document during an Internet outage. Explain a benefit and a limitation of cloud storage. [4 marks]
Benefit: access remotely from different devices [1], allowing work at school/home [1]. Limitation: requires availability of connection/provider [1], so data may be temporarily inaccessible [1].
